metadata.title: Shape the first QuickerGrillMe release
metadata.description: Confirm only the choices that materially change product behavior, architecture, cost, or risk. Every question starts with an Agent recommendation.

questions.prompt: What should the first release optimize for?

options.label: Fast consequential decisions
options.description: Minimize effort while surfacing choices that materially alter the design.

options.label: Maximum issue coverage
options.description: Favor broader interrogation even when many answers are unlikely to change the design.

options.label: Documentation completeness
options.description: Optimize primarily for producing a comprehensive written artifact.

questions.recommendationRationale: The product is differentiated by disciplined restraint rather than exhaustive questioning.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if users frequently add major decisions after completing the questionnaire.

questions.prompt: Who is the primary v1 operator?

options.label: Agent-assisted developer
options.description: A developer and coding Agent collaborate on a design before implementation.

options.label: Cross-functional product team
options.description: Several people jointly answer and approve the questionnaire.

options.label: Autonomous Agent
options.description: The Agent uses the workflow without a person reviewing every answer.

questions.recommendationRationale: The browser review and local artifact workflow are designed for a developer-Agent pair.

defer.validationTrigger: Validate with the first five real workflows and note who actually edits answers.

questions.prompt: Which responsibility belongs outside the v1 core?

options.label: Final design generation
options.description: The core captures decisions; the calling Agent writes the final design document.

options.label: Question generation
options.description: The core only displays a fully prepared questionnaire.

options.label: Nothing
options.description: The core generates questions, collects answers, and writes the final design.

questions.recommendationRationale: Keeping prose generation with the Agent preserves a language-agnostic, lightweight core.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit when a second Agent integration cannot reliably consume answers.json.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum evidence that the questionnaire is working?

options.label: Material design changes
options.description: Changed answers lead to visibly different architecture, behavior, cost, or risk decisions.

options.label: High completion rate
options.description: Most users submit the questionnaire without abandoning it.

options.label: Questions answered
options.description: Success is measured mainly by the number of issues considered.

questions.recommendationRationale: The counterfactual test is the product's core quality bar.

defer.validationTrigger: Compare recommendation changes with resulting design diffs across ten uses.

questions.prompt: How should users complete the questionnaire in v1?

options.label: Local browser form
options.description: A local-only server renders a focused multi-page questionnaire.

options.label: Terminal prompts
options.description: Questions are presented sequentially in the command line.

options.label: Hosted web application
options.description: A remote service stores questionnaires and responses.

questions.recommendationRationale: A local form reduces conversational overhead without introducing service infrastructure.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if target Agent environments cannot open or reach a loopback URL.

questions.prompt: Where should submitted answers be stored?

options.label: Local JSON artifact
options.description: Write a portable answers.json file chosen by the caller.

options.label: Memory only
options.description: Return answers to the current process without a persistent artifact.

options.label: Database
options.description: Store responses in a managed local or remote database.

questions.recommendationRationale: JSON is inspectable, language-neutral, versionable, and easy for an Agent to consume.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if concurrent editing or response history becomes a requirement.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a questionnaire is structurally invalid?

options.label: Fail with actionable errors
options.description: Do not launch; report every safely detectable schema and dependency issue.

options.label: Render best effort
options.description: Skip invalid fields and show whatever can still be interpreted.

options.label: Repair automatically
options.description: Mutate invalid input into a form the adapter can render.

questions.recommendationRationale: Silent repairs can conceal design omissions and produce success-shaped but unreliable output.

defer.validationTrigger: Review validation failures after several generated questionnaires for overly strict rules.

questions.prompt: Does the local browser need multi-user collaboration?

options.label: Single local user
options.description: One browser session completes one answer artifact.

options.label: Shared live session
options.description: Multiple people can edit the same questionnaire concurrently.

options.label: Shareable review only
options.description: One person edits while others receive an exported review artifact.

questions.recommendationRationale: Collaboration infrastructure would dominate the first release without proving the core decision model.

defer.validationTrigger: Track requests to co-edit the same questionnaire during early usage.

questions.prompt: How should additional user interfaces integrate with the core?

options.label: JSON contract and adapter interface
options.description: Adapters consume questionnaire JSON and produce answers JSON.

options.label: TypeScript API only
options.description: Adapters link directly against the reference implementation.

options.label: HTTP API
options.description: All integrations communicate with a long-running service.

questions.recommendationRationale: Language-neutral artifacts preserve cross-Agent portability while TypeScript remains the reference.

defer.validationTrigger: Implement a second adapter and record any contract gaps.

questions.prompt: How should upstream answer changes affect dependent questions?

options.label: Recompute and hide invalidated questions
options.description: Re-evaluate visibility and ordering while retaining hidden answers in memory.

options.label: Freeze the initial form
options.description: Keep all originally shown questions regardless of answer changes.

options.label: Recompute and discard
options.description: Remove answers for every question that becomes hidden.

questions.recommendationRationale: Dynamic visibility respects the decision DAG while retaining work if a user changes back.

defer.validationTrigger: Observe whether hidden retained answers surprise users during submission review.

questions.prompt: What should trigger a second question round?

options.label: Conflicts, invalid premises, or high-risk unknowns
options.description: Ask at most 3–5 follow-ups only when one of the explicit risk triggers remains.

options.label: Any changed recommendation
options.description: Follow up whenever the user differs from an Agent recommendation.

options.label: Always ask a second round
options.description: Use a confirmation round after every initial submission.

questions.recommendationRationale: A changed answer is informative but does not itself justify more questioning.

defer.validationTrigger: Revisit if consequential contradictions regularly escape round one.

questions.prompt: What sensitivity should the local artifacts assume?

options.label: Internal design information
options.description: May contain non-public architecture details but no secrets or customer content.

options.label: Public information only
options.description: Questionnaires are safe to publish without review.

options.label: Restricted or customer data
options.description: Artifacts may contain regulated, secret, or customer-provided content.

questions.recommendationRationale: Local-only storage reduces exposure, but generated design inputs commonly contain internal details.

defer.validationTrigger: Classify representative questionnaires under the adopting organization's data policy.

questions.prompt: What operational signal is needed in v1?

options.label: Clear local console events
options.description: Report URL, validation failures, submission path, and shutdown.

options.label: Structured local logs
options.description: Persist machine-readable request and lifecycle events.

options.label: Remote telemetry
options.description: Send usage and performance data to a managed service.

questions.recommendationRationale: Lifecycle clarity is sufficient for a short-lived local process and avoids data collection.

defer.validationTrigger: Add structured logs if failures cannot be diagnosed from CLI output.

questions.prompt: How should contract changes be introduced?

options.label: Explicit schema version
options.description: Reject unsupported major versions and evolve minor fields compatibly.

options.label: Best-effort compatibility
options.description: Ignore unknown fields and infer missing ones where possible.

options.label: Package lockstep
options.description: Require producer and adapter to use exactly the same release.

questions.recommendationRationale: Artifacts can outlive a process, so version intent must travel with the data.

defer.validationTrigger: Define migration rules before shipping the first breaking contract change.

questions.prompt: How should simultaneous edits be reconciled?

options.label: Last write wins
options.description: The latest accepted update replaces earlier state.

options.label: Optimistic locking
options.description: Reject stale updates and ask the editor to reconcile.

options.label: Field-level merge
options.description: Combine non-overlapping updates and surface direct conflicts.

questions.recommendationRationale: If collaboration is selected, explicit conflict handling is safer than silent overwrite.

defer.validationTrigger: Prototype with two concurrent editors before committing to a collaboration model.

questions.prompt: When should visibility conditions be re-evaluated?

options.label: After every answer change
options.description: Refresh pages immediately from current answer values.

options.label: On page transition
options.description: Keep the current page stable and recompute before navigation.

options.label: Only at submission
options.description: Validate dependencies after the user finishes all visible pages.

questions.recommendationRationale: The local dataset is small, and immediate feedback prevents users answering invalidated questions.

defer.validationTrigger: Measure responsiveness on a 25-question deep questionnaire.

questions.prompt: Should users be able to submit unanswered visible questions?

options.label: Only with explicit defer
options.description: Every visible question is answered or carries a temporary default and validation trigger.

options.label: Allow empty answers
options.description: Missing answers are accepted without a recorded default.

options.label: Require high-impact only
options.description: Lower-impact questions can remain empty.

questions.recommendationRationale: Explicit defer distinguishes intentional uncertainty from accidental omission.

defer.validationTrigger: Review whether mandatory low-impact answers create avoidable friction.

questions.prompt: What accessibility baseline should the browser adapter meet?

options.label: Semantic and keyboard operable
options.description: Use native controls, visible focus, labels, and screen-reader-friendly status updates.

options.label: Visual usability only
options.description: Prioritize pointer-based desktop interaction for the prototype.

options.label: Formal WCAG AA audit
options.description: Block release on a full independent conformance assessment.

questions.recommendationRationale: Native controls provide a strong lightweight baseline without turning v1 into a compliance program.

defer.validationTrigger: Run keyboard and screen-reader smoke tests before the first tagged release.

questions.prompt: What is the most important local-server threat to address?

options.label: Accidental network exposure
options.description: Bind only to loopback and avoid external resources.

options.label: Malicious questionnaire content
options.description: Prevent generated prompts from executing as browser markup or script.

options.label: Arbitrary local file access
options.description: Constrain output paths and static file serving.

questions.recommendationRationale: Loopback-only binding is the primary architectural security boundary; safe DOM rendering remains mandatory.

defer.validationTrigger: Perform a focused threat review before distributing the CLI beyond local development.

questions.prompt: How long should the tool retain submitted answers?

options.label: Caller-owned lifecycle
options.description: Write the requested file and leave retention to the repository or workspace policy.

options.label: Automatic deletion
options.description: Delete answers after the Agent consumes them.

options.label: Built-in response history
options.description: Retain timestamped submissions for comparison.

questions.recommendationRationale: A CLI should not silently delete or retain artifacts outside the caller's established workflow.

defer.validationTrigger: Document adopting-team retention expectations before handling restricted data.

questions.prompt: How should the core handle a dependency cycle?

options.label: Reject with cycle members
options.description: Fail validation and identify the questions participating in the cycle.

options.label: Fall back to source order
options.description: Ignore dependency edges when a cycle is found.

options.label: Remove an edge automatically
options.description: Break the cycle using a deterministic but implicit rule.

questions.recommendationRationale: A cycle represents ambiguous decision prerequisites and should be repaired by the questionnaire producer.

defer.validationTrigger: Review generated cycle errors to improve Agent-side questionnaire construction.

questions.prompt: How should the reference implementation be distributed first?

options.label: Node CLI package
options.description: Build to JavaScript and expose a conventional executable.

options.label: Source checkout only
options.description: Require TypeScript tooling and repository access.

options.label: Standalone binary
options.description: Bundle a platform-specific executable.

questions.recommendationRationale: The target environments already run Agents with Node, and package distribution adds little machinery.

defer.validationTrigger: Validate installation friction in one environment that does not have a TypeScript toolchain.
